items.title: Leveraging Frequency Analysis for Deep Fake Image Recognition
items.venue: ICML 2020 (37th International Conference on Machine Learning), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research
items.method_category: DCT-spectrum artifact analysis + linear/CNN classifiers
items.research_question: Do GAN-generated images carry systematic artifacts in the frequency (DCT) domain that allow reliable and simple detection?
items.key_idea: Shows that upsampling in GAN generators produces consistent grid-like artifacts in the 2D DCT spectrum; even linear models on log-scaled DCT coefficients separate real from GAN images and attribute the source GAN.
items.dataset: GAN images trained on FFHQ, CelebA and LSUN Bedroom (see paper for exact generator list)
items.limitations: Evaluated on GAN generators of 2017-2019; spectral cues may weaken under compression/resizing and on diffusion models with different upsampling paths.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Directly motivates a NumPy DCT/FFT spectral-fingerprint module (log-DCT heatmaps, peak statistics) in SynthProvenance.

items.title: Watch Your Up-Convolution: CNN Based Generative Deep Neural Networks Are Failing to Reproduce Spectral Distributions
items.venue: CVPR 2020 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)
items.method_category: Azimuthally averaged power spectrum features + spectral regularization
items.research_question: Why do up-convolution based generators fail to reproduce the spectral distribution of natural images, and can this be exploited for detection?
items.key_idea: Up-convolution/transposed-convolution layers distort the high-frequency spectrum; a 1D azimuthally averaged power spectrum with a simple classifier detects fakes, and a spectral regularization term during training reduces the artifact.
items.dataset: Face image datasets with GAN fakes (e.g., CelebA; see paper for full list)
items.limitations: Simple spectral features can be defeated by spectral regularization (as the paper itself shows) and by post-processing such as JPEG compression or resizing.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Provides the classic 1D radial power-spectrum fingerprint that SynthProvenance can compute with NumPy FFT as a baseline spectral cue.

items.title: Attributing Fake Images to GANs: Learning and Analyzing GAN Fingerprints
items.venue: ICCV 2019 (IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision)
items.method_category: Learned model/image fingerprints + attribution classifier
items.research_question: Do GANs leave stable, model-specific fingerprints that allow attributing a fake image to the exact GAN instance that produced it?
items.key_idea: Trains an attribution network that jointly learns per-model fingerprints and per-image fingerprints; shows that even small differences in architecture, seed or training data yield distinguishable fingerprints.
items.dataset: CelebA and LSUN Bedroom with ProGAN, SNGAN, CramerGAN, MMDGAN (see paper)
items.limitations: Closed-set attribution over a fixed set of GAN instances; robustness to unseen generators and diffusion models is not addressed.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Foundational definition of model vs. image fingerprints that SynthProvenance's attribution layer builds on.

items.title: Artificial Fingerprinting for Generative Models: Rooting Deepfake Attribution in Training Data
items.venue: ICCV 2021 (IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision)
items.method_category: Steganographic fingerprint embedded in training data, transferred to the generator
items.research_question: Can an artificial fingerprint embedded into training data be inherited by a generative model so that its outputs become attributable?
items.key_idea: Embeds a learned steganographic code into all training images; GANs trained on this data reproduce the code in generated images, which a decoder recovers for proactive attribution.
items.dataset: CelebA, LSUN and other image benchmarks (see paper)
items.limitations: Requires control over the training data of the generator; robustness against deliberate removal and fine-tuning is only partially analysed.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Represents the 'training-data watermark' branch of proactive provenance that SynthProvenance should distinguish from post-hoc watermarks.

items.title: Deepfake Network Architecture Attribution
items.venue: AAAI 2022 (Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence)
items.method_category: Architecture-level attribution via patch-wise contrastive learning (DNA-Det)
items.research_question: Can fake images be attributed to the generator architecture even when weights, seeds or training data differ?
items.key_idea: Argues that architecture leaves globally consistent local traces; DNA-Det uses pre-training on image-transformation classification and patch-wise contrastive learning to obtain architecture-level fingerprints.
items.dataset: GAN images from multiple architectures and training configurations (see paper)
items.limitations: Focused on GAN architectures; transfer to diffusion and autoregressive generators is not established in the paper.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Supports an architecture-level (coarse) attribution tier in SynthProvenance, complementary to instance-level fingerprints.

items.title: Learning to Disentangle GAN Fingerprint for Fake Image Attribution
items.venue: arXiv preprint
items.method_category: Fingerprint/content disentangling network (GFD-Net), multi-task
items.research_question: Can a GAN fingerprint be explicitly disentangled from image content to give interpretable, content-irrelevant attribution features?
items.key_idea: GFD-Net jointly extracts a fingerprint image and a content-irrelevant representation, with constraints for stability and discriminability, and analyses which GAN components dominate the fingerprint.
items.dataset: GAN-generated image sets for closed- and open-world attribution (see paper)
items.limitations: Preprint without a located peer-reviewed version; evaluated on GANs only.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Motivates showing an explicit 'fingerprint residual' visualization separate from content in the SynthProvenance UI.

items.title: Disentangling different levels of GAN fingerprints for task-specific forensics
items.venue: Computer Standards & Interfaces (Elsevier)
items.method_category: Two-level fingerprint decoupling across signal domains + adversarial augmentation
items.research_question: Can GAN fingerprints be separated into different levels so that each level serves a different forensic task?
items.key_idea: Based on a fingerprint-dependency analysis indicating two fingerprint levels residing in different signal domains, proposes a decoupling representation framework with adversarial data augmentation and a transformation-invariant loss for robustness.
items.dataset: GAN-generated image benchmarks (see paper)
items.limitations: GAN-only evaluation; abstract-level details were obtained from a repository abstract because the publisher page was not accessible.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Supports a multi-level fingerprint design (e.g., family-level vs. model-level) in SynthProvenance's taxonomy.

items.title: DIRE for Diffusion-Generated Image Detection
items.venue: ICCV 2023 (IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision)
items.method_category: Diffusion reconstruction error (DDIM inversion + reconstruction) + CNN classifier
items.research_question: Can the error between an image and its reconstruction by a pre-trained diffusion model separate diffusion-generated from real images?
items.key_idea: Generated images are reconstructed more faithfully by a diffusion model than real images; the DIffusion Reconstruction Error (DIRE) map is used as input to a binary classifier.
items.dataset: DiffusionForensics (introduced in the paper)
items.limitations: Expensive (inversion per image) and later work reports sensitivity to JPEG/format biases in the training data; behaviour on latent diffusion models depends on the reconstruction model used.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Canonical reconstruction-error signal; SynthProvenance can expose it as an optional DL-runtime module.

items.title: AEROBLADE: Training-Free Detection of Latent Diffusion Images Using Autoencoder Reconstruction Error
items.venue: CVPR 2024 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)
items.method_category: Training-free LDM autoencoder reconstruction error (LPIPS-based)
items.research_question: Can latent-diffusion images be detected without training by measuring how well the LDM's autoencoder reconstructs them?
items.key_idea: Images produced by an LDM lie close to its autoencoder's decoder manifold, so their AE reconstruction error (measured with an LPIPS-style distance) is lower than for real images; the minimum over candidate AEs also gives attribution.
items.dataset: Images from Stable Diffusion variants, Kandinsky, Midjourney and real images (see paper)
items.limitations: Requires access to the candidate generator's autoencoder; robustness to strong compression and to non-LDM generators is limited.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: A training-free, attribution-capable reconstruction signal well suited to SynthProvenance's 'explainable evidence' panel.

items.title: ManiFPT: Defining and Analyzing Fingerprints of Generative Models
items.venue: CVPR 2024 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)
items.method_category: Manifold-based formal definition of artifacts/fingerprints + attribution
items.research_question: What exactly is a generative-model fingerprint, and can a formal definition improve model attribution across many generator types?
items.key_idea: Formalizes an artifact as the deviation of a generated sample from the real-data manifold and a fingerprint as the distribution of these artifacts, gives a practical algorithm to compute them, and shows improved attribution over a large array of generators.
items.dataset: Samples from a large array of generative models (GANs, VAEs, flows, diffusion; see paper)
items.limitations: Requires an estimate of the real-data manifold (e.g., via a learned embedding), so results depend on that estimator and reference dataset.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Provides a principled definition of 'fingerprint' that SynthProvenance's documentation and taxonomy can adopt.

items.title: Causal Fingerprints of AI Generative Models
items.venue: ICASSP 2026 (IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing); preprint arXiv:2509.15406 (2025)
items.method_category: Causality-decoupling of fingerprint from content/style in a diffusion-residual latent space
items.research_question: Can a model fingerprint be defined causally, i.e., as the component of image traces that is caused by the generator rather than by content or style?
items.key_idea: Introduces the 'causal fingerprint' and a causality-decoupling framework that separates it from image-specific content and style in a semantic-invariant latent space derived from pre-trained diffusion reconstruction residuals; validated via attribution and counterfactual source anonymization.
items.dataset: Representative GAN and diffusion model outputs (see paper)
items.limitations: Short (5-page) conference paper; causal claims rest on the proposed decoupling framework and counterfactual experiments rather than formal identifiability guarantees.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Core reference for SynthProvenance's CAUSAL fingerprint category and counterfactual explanations.

items.title: ProMark: Proactive Diffusion Watermarking for Causal Attribution
items.venue: CVPR 2024 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)
items.method_category: Concept watermarks embedded in training images, retained by diffusion models
items.research_question: Can a generated image be causally attributed to training-data concepts (objects, styles, artists) by proactively watermarking the training data?
items.key_idea: Embeds imperceptible concept-specific watermarks (up to 2^16 unique codes, possibly several per image) into training images; diffusion models trained on them reproduce the watermarks, enabling causal rather than correlation-based attribution.
items.dataset: Concept-labelled image datasets for training-data attribution (see paper)
items.limitations: Requires watermarking the training corpus before model training; robustness against adaptive removal is not the paper's main focus.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Links proactive watermarking with causal attribution, bridging SynthProvenance's PROACTIVE_WATERMARK and CAUSAL categories.

items.title: The Stable Signature: Rooting Watermarks in Latent Diffusion Models
items.venue: ICCV 2023 (IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision)
items.method_category: Fine-tuning the LDM decoder to embed a fixed signature decoded by a pre-trained extractor
items.research_question: Can a watermark be rooted in a latent diffusion model so that every generated image carries an identifying signature?
items.key_idea: Fine-tunes the LDM's VAE decoder so that all outputs embed a fixed binary signature recoverable by a pre-trained (HiDDeN-style) extractor, enabling detection and user identification with controlled false-positive rates.
items.dataset: Stable Diffusion generations from text prompts (e.g., MS-COCO captions; see paper)
items.limitations: Signature sits in the decoder and can be removed by swapping/fine-tuning the decoder or by regeneration attacks (see Zhao et al., 2024; WAVES).
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Reference in-model watermark that SynthProvenance should be able to report and contrast with post-hoc watermarks.

items.title: Tree-Rings Watermarks: Invisible Fingerprints for Diffusion Images
items.venue: NeurIPS 2023 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36); preprint arXiv:2305.20030
items.method_category: Fourier-space key pattern in the initial noise; detection via DDIM inversion
items.research_question: Can diffusion outputs be watermarked invisibly and robustly by modifying only the initial noise rather than post-processing the image?
items.key_idea: Embeds a ring-shaped key in the Fourier transform of the initial noise latent; the watermark is detected by inverting the image back to noise (DDIM inversion) and testing for the key pattern.
items.dataset: Stable Diffusion and ImageNet guided-diffusion generations (see paper)
items.limitations: Detection requires the model for inversion; later work shows forgery and removal attacks on such semantic watermarks (e.g., Müller et al., CVPR 2025).
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Prototype of 'semantic' in-generation watermarks; SynthProvenance should model its detection as model-dependent evidence.

items.title: Gaussian Shading: Provable Performance-Lossless Image Watermarking for Diffusion Models
items.venue: CVPR 2024 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)
items.method_category: Distribution-preserving sampling of the initial latent from the watermark bits
items.research_question: Can a diffusion watermark be embedded without any change to the output distribution (performance-lossless) while remaining robust?
items.key_idea: Maps (diffused and randomized) watermark bits to a Gaussian initial latent via distribution-preserving sampling, so watermarked latents follow the same distribution as unwatermarked ones; extraction uses DDIM inversion.
items.dataset: Stable Diffusion generations (see paper)
items.limitations: Extraction depends on accurate inversion; shown to be vulnerable to black-box forgery/removal attacks on semantic watermarks (Müller et al., CVPR 2025).
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Key example of latent-space semantic watermarks for SynthProvenance's watermark-robustness comparisons.

items.title: Towards Universal Fake Image Detectors That Generalize Across Generative Models
items.venue: CVPR 2023 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)

items.venue: CVPR 2025 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)
items.method_category: Self-supervised masked spectral learning; spectral reconstruction similarity; spectral context attention (SPAI)

items.limitations: Requires a trained deep model; robustness to aggressive compression and resizing pipelines is reported but not exhaustive.

items.title: Do GANs Leave Artificial Fingerprints?
items.venue: IEEE MIPR 2019 (Conference on Multimedia Information Processing and Retrieval)
items.method_category: PRNU-style averaged noise residuals per GAN + correlation-based attribution
items.research_question: Do GANs leave stable, model-specific traces analogous to camera PRNU fingerprints?
items.key_idea: Averages high-pass noise residuals of many images from one GAN to estimate its fingerprint and attributes images by correlating their residuals with these fingerprints, mirroring PRNU camera identification.
items.dataset: Images from several GAN architectures/training sets (see paper)
items.limitations: Small-scale study on early GANs; residual fingerprints are weakened by compression and resizing.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Directly maps to a NumPy residual-averaging + normalized-correlation fingerprint module in SynthProvenance.

items.dataset: ForenSynths (ProGAN training set; test set of 11 CNN-based generators)
items.limitations: Generalization is limited to CNN-based generators of that era and drops on diffusion models, as later studies show.

items.title: Detecting and Simulating Artifacts in GAN Fake Images
items.venue: IEEE WIFS 2019 (International Workshop on Information Forensics and Security)
items.method_category: Spectrum-based classifier + AutoGAN artifact simulator
items.research_question: Can the up-sampling artifacts common to GAN pipelines be detected in the frequency domain and simulated without access to the GANs?
items.key_idea: Shows up-sampling causes spectral replications; trains a classifier on spectra and proposes AutoGAN, a simulator that reproduces these artifacts from real images so detectors can be trained without GAN samples.
items.dataset: CycleGAN-style image-to-image translation fakes (see paper)
items.limitations: Targets up-sampling artifacts of GAN-era generators; classifier relies on training data and may not transfer to diffusion models.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Supports SynthProvenance's spectral-replication visualization and the idea of simulated-artifact training data.

items.title: On the Frequency Bias of Generative Models
items.venue: NeurIPS 2021 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34)
items.method_category: Controlled study of generator/discriminator components causing spectral artifacts
items.research_question: Which components of GAN training (generator upsampling, discriminator, losses) cause the spectral discrepancies of generated images, and can proposed fixes remove them?
items.key_idea: Systematically analyses sources of the frequency bias and finds that proposed spectral losses/discriminators do not fully eliminate high-frequency artifacts, highlighting the role of the generator's upsampling.
items.dataset: Toy and real image datasets (e.g., FFHQ-type faces; see paper)
items.limitations: Analysis centred on GANs; implications for diffusion models are not directly tested.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Explains why spectral fingerprints exist, informing which frequency bands SynthProvenance inspects.

items.title: On the use of Benford's law to detect GAN-generated images
items.venue: ICPR 2020 (25th International Conference on Pattern Recognition; held January 2021)
items.method_category: First-digit (Benford) statistics of DCT coefficients + classifier
items.research_question: Do the first-digit statistics of block-DCT coefficients of GAN images deviate from Benford's law in a way usable for detection?
items.key_idea: Computes divergences between the empirical first-digit distribution of DCT coefficients and a generalized Benford law, and uses them as compact features for GAN-image detection.
items.dataset: GAN-generated vs. real image sets (see paper)
items.limitations: Hand-crafted statistics that can be perturbed by JPEG re-compression and post-processing; evaluated on GANs.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Lightweight NumPy-implementable statistical feature for SynthProvenance's interpretable baseline set.

items.title: Rethinking the Up-Sampling Operations in CNN-based Generative Network for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
items.venue: CVPR 2024 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)
items.method_category: Neighboring Pixel Relationships (NPR) residual from up-sampling + CNN detector
items.research_question: Can a simple representation of local pixel dependencies created by up-sampling serve as a generalizable artifact across GANs and diffusion models?
items.key_idea: Up-sampling creates characteristic correlations between neighbouring pixels; NPR captures them (difference between an image and its down-up-sampled version) and a lightweight classifier trained on them generalizes across many generators.
items.dataset: ForenSynths-style training (ProGAN) and many unseen GAN/diffusion test sets (see paper)
items.limitations: Depends on up-sampling traces that can be weakened by resizing or JPEG compression; reported robustness to post-processing is limited.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: NPR residual is cheap to compute in NumPy and is a strong candidate for SynthProvenance's spatial-artifact features.

items.title: Digital Camera Identification From Sensor Pattern Noise
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
items.method_category: PRNU sensor-noise fingerprint via wavelet denoising residuals + correlation detector
items.research_question: Can a digital camera be identified from the photo-response non-uniformity (PRNU) noise pattern in its images?
items.key_idea: Estimates a camera reference pattern by averaging wavelet-denoising residuals of many images and identifies the source camera by correlating a test image's residual with that pattern.
items.dataset: Images from multiple consumer digital cameras (see paper)
items.limitations: Designed for physical camera sensors; geometric transforms and strong compression reduce correlation.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Methodological template for generator 'fingerprints' (residual averaging + correlation) implemented in NumPy in SynthProvenance.

items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

items.key_idea: Builds a rich model from many linear and non-linear high-pass residual filters, quantized co-occurrence statistics and an ensemble classifier; the SRM filters became standard pre-processing in image forensics.

items.limitations: Very high-dimensional hand-crafted features; designed for steganalysis rather than generative-model forensics.

items.title: Secure spread spectrum watermarking for multimedia
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Image Processing
items.method_category: Spread-spectrum watermark in perceptually significant DCT coefficients
items.research_question: How can a watermark be embedded so that it is robust to common signal processing and collusion while remaining imperceptible?
items.key_idea: Spreads an i.i.d. Gaussian watermark over the perceptually most significant DCT coefficients and detects it by correlation with the original, giving robustness to compression, filtering and other distortions.
items.limitations: Non-blind detection (original image needed) in the basic scheme; not designed against modern learned removal attacks.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Foundational, NumPy-implementable watermark used as a classical baseline in SynthProvenance's watermark module.

items.title: HiDDeN: Hiding Data With Deep Networks
items.venue: ECCV 2018 (European Conference on Computer Vision), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, Springer
items.method_category: End-to-end CNN encoder/decoder with differentiable noise layers
items.research_question: Can deep networks learn to embed and robustly recover hidden messages in images, including under distortions?
items.key_idea: Jointly trains encoder, decoder and adversary with differentiable noise layers (crop, dropout, Gaussian blur, JPEG approximation) so that embedded bits survive distortions while remaining imperceptible.
items.dataset: COCO images (see paper)
items.limitations: Robustness is limited to the distortions modelled during training; regeneration attacks remove such pixel-level watermarks.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Architecture underlying many learned watermark extractors (e.g., used by Stable Signature); baseline for SynthProvenance robustness tests.

items.limitations: Visible-ish artifacts at high strength; vulnerable to regeneration attacks shown in later benchmarks (e.g., WAVES).

items.title: WAVES: Benchmarking the Robustness of Image Watermarks
items.venue: ICML 2024 (41st International Conference on Machine Learning), PMLR
items.method_category: Standardized watermark robustness benchmark (distortion, regeneration, adversarial attacks)
items.research_question: How robust are current image watermarks under a standardized, diverse set of removal attacks and evaluation protocols?
items.key_idea: Proposes WAVES, a benchmark that evaluates watermarks (e.g., Tree-Ring, Stable Signature, StegaStamp) against distortion, regeneration and adversarial attacks with standardized quality/performance metrics.
items.dataset: DiffusionDB, MS-COCO and DALL-E 3 image sets (see paper)

items.title: A Sanity Check for AI-generated Image Detection
items.venue: ICLR 2025 (International Conference on Learning Representations)
items.method_category: Hybrid low-level (frequency/patch) + high-level (CLIP) feature detector (AIDE) + Chameleon dataset
items.research_question: Do current AI-image detectors still work on highly realistic images that humans misjudge as real?
items.key_idea: Introduces the Chameleon dataset of human-deceiving AI images and AIDE, a detector that combines low-level patch/frequency statistics with high-level CLIP semantics, showing that existing detectors struggle on Chameleon.
items.dataset: Chameleon (introduced), AIGCDetectBenchmark, GenImage
items.limitations: Even the proposed detector leaves substantial errors on Chameleon, indicating the problem is far from solved.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Provides a hard, realistic test set and a hybrid design pattern for SynthProvenance's evidence fusion.

items.title: Forensic Self-Descriptions Are All You Need for Zero-Shot Detection, Open-Set Source Attribution, and Clustering of AI-generated Images
items.venue: CVPR 2025 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)
items.method_category: Self-supervised predictive-filter residuals modelled per image (forensic self-description)
items.research_question: Can a per-image model of forensic microstructures, learned only from real images, support zero-shot detection and open-set attribution?
items.key_idea: Learns diverse predictive filters on real images to extract multi-scale residuals; the parameters of a compact model fitted to these residuals form a 'forensic self-description' used for zero-shot detection, open-set source attribution and clustering.
items.dataset: Real images plus outputs of many GAN and diffusion generators (see paper)
items.limitations: Microstructure cues can be degraded by strong compression or resizing; per-image model fitting adds computation.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Closely matches SynthProvenance's goal of training-free, open-set fingerprinting from residual statistics.

items.title: A Bias-Free Training Paradigm for More General AI-generated Image Detection
items.venue: CVPR 2025 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)
items.method_category: Bias-free training data via SD self-conditioned regeneration + content augmentation (B-Free)
items.research_question: Can AI-image detectors generalize better if training data are constructed so that real and fake images differ only in generation artifacts?
items.key_idea: Generates fake training images from real ones via Stable Diffusion's conditioning (semantically aligned pairs) and uses content-based augmentation, reducing content/format biases and improving generalization and calibration across 27 generators.
items.dataset: Real images and SD-regenerated counterparts; evaluation on 27 generators and social-network data (see paper)
items.limitations: Training relies on Stable Diffusion artifacts; generalization to very different generator families still needs monitoring.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Guides how SynthProvenance should build bias-controlled training/evaluation sets.

items.title: Black-Box Forgery Attacks on Semantic Watermarks for Diffusion Models
items.venue: CVPR 2025 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)
items.method_category: Latent-space imprinting and reprompting forgery attacks using unrelated LDMs
items.research_question: Are semantic watermarks such as Tree-Ring and Gaussian Shading secure against forgery by attackers using unrelated diffusion models?
items.key_idea: Shows that an attacker with a single watermarked image and an unrelated LDM (even with different latent space/architecture) can imprint the watermark into real images or regenerate new watermarked images, and can also remove watermarks.
items.dataset: Watermarked Stable Diffusion/DiT outputs and real images (see paper)
items.limitations: Targets semantic (initial-noise) watermarks; post-hoc and in-decoder watermarks need separate analysis.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Warns that a detected semantic watermark in SynthProvenance cannot by itself prove origin; spoofing must be considered.

items.title: FIRE: Robust Detection of Diffusion-Generated Images via Frequency-Guided Reconstruction Error
items.venue: CVPR 2025 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)
items.method_category: Change of diffusion reconstruction error before/after mid-band frequency decomposition
items.research_question: Can the difficulty diffusion models have in reconstructing mid-band frequencies of real images be used for robust detection?
items.key_idea: Observes that diffusion models reconstruct mid-frequency content of real images poorly and measures the variation in reconstruction error before and after frequency decomposition (with a learned frequency mask) as a detection cue.
items.dataset: Diffusion-generated image benchmarks such as DiffusionForensics (see paper)
items.limitations: Requires diffusion reconstruction at inference time, which is computationally heavy.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Bridges SynthProvenance's RECONSTRUCTION and SPECTRAL categories in a single cue.

items.title: Riemannian-Geometric Fingerprints of Generative Models
items.venue: ICCV 2025 (IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision)
items.method_category: Riemannian-geometric definition of artifacts/fingerprints + attribution
items.research_question: Can fingerprints of generative models be defined and analysed in a principled way using Riemannian geometry?
items.key_idea: Generalizes the manifold-based fingerprint definition (ManiFPT) using Riemannian geometry, providing a formal framework to define, represent and analyse model fingerprints for attribution.
items.dataset: Outputs of diverse generative models across datasets and modalities (see paper)
items.limitations: Geometry estimation depends on learned embeddings and reference data; computational cost is higher than simple residual methods.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Theoretical successor to ManiFPT that informs SynthProvenance's formal fingerprint definitions.

items.title: TrustMark: Robust Watermarking and Watermark Removal for Arbitrary Resolution Images
items.venue: ICCV 2025 (IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision)
items.method_category: Post-hoc learned watermark with spatio-spectral loss + ReMark removal, resolution-agnostic
items.research_question: Can a post-hoc watermark be both high-fidelity and robust for images of any resolution, with a controlled removal mechanism for re-watermarking?
items.key_idea: TrustMark uses a spatio-spectral loss and a 1x1 convolution layer to improve encoding quality (PSNR above 43 dB) and robustness; ReMark removes watermarks for re-watermarking, and a simple scheme extends both to arbitrary resolutions.
items.dataset: Three watermarking benchmarks (see paper)
items.limitations: Post-hoc watermark that remains exposed to regeneration attacks studied in WAVES and Zhao et al. (2024).
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Open-source (MIT) watermark associated with provenance workflows; SynthProvenance can use it as a soft-binding signal alongside C2PA manifests.

items.title: Learning Counterfactually Decoupled Attention for Open-World Model Attribution
items.venue: ICCV 2025 (IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision)
items.method_category: Counterfactual attention decoupling of model-specific artifacts from source biases (CDAL)
items.research_question: Can causal modelling of attention improve open-world attribution to unseen source models?
items.key_idea: Models causal relations between attentional visual traces and source attribution, counterfactually decoupling model-specific artifacts from confounding biases and maximizing the resulting causal effect to learn generalizable attention.
items.dataset: Open-world model attribution benchmarks (see paper)
items.limitations: Causal effect is estimated within the network via counterfactual attention, not via interventions on real generators.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Second CAUSAL-category reference showing how counterfactual reasoning improves open-set attribution in SynthProvenance.

items.title: Attribution as Retrieval: Model-Agnostic AI-Generated Image Attribution
items.venue: CVPR 2026 (IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition)
items.method_category: Low-bit-plane fingerprints + unsupervised pre-training + few-shot retrieval-based attribution (LIDA)
items.research_question: Can AI-generated image attribution be made model-agnostic and scalable to new generators by casting it as instance retrieval?
items.key_idea: LIDA extracts low-bit-plane fingerprints, learns embeddings with unsupervised pre-training and few-shot attribution, and attributes images by retrieval rather than closed-set classification.
items.dataset: AI-generated image attribution benchmarks (see paper)
items.limitations: Recent (2026) work without independent replication; low-bit-plane cues may be fragile under lossy compression.
items.synthprovenance_relevance: Retrieval-style open-set attribution matches SynthProvenance's need to add new generators without retraining.
